# remuda-driver fixtures

- `instance-spec.json` — copied from `crates/remuda-protocol/tests/fixtures/instance-spec.json` (`protocol.md` §4.1).
- `claude-print-stream.jsonl` — 23 ordered stdout frames recorded on 2026-09-13 from a real `remuda dev` Claude print session with `--include-partial-messages`. The short Chinese prompt asked why streaming replies should merge into one message. This preserves the actual delta boundaries, empty thinking block, singleton assistant snapshots before each `content_block_stop`, and final result. Native message identity is replaced by `msg_recorded_stream_1`; per-frame UUIDs are distinct deterministic placeholders because the sanitized capture omitted the original identifiers. Thinking signature material is replaced by `recorded-signature-redacted`. No credentials, personal paths, or native account/session identifiers are retained. Live before/after evidence is in `docs/design/evidence/print-stream-1.md`.
- `claude-sdk-partial-then-final.jsonl` — 20 ordered stdout frames **generated by Remuda** (hand-written to the shapes `claude-print-stream.jsonl` recorded live, then replayed through `map_outbound` to confirm the assembler accepts them) for the `claude-sdk` carrier's partial-vs-final assertions. No live session, no billed model, and no bytes from the Anthropic CLI or extension bundle were used (`print-replacement.md` §3 fixture strategy, §4.3). It holds one turn whose native message id `msg_recorded_sdk_1` spans a `thinking` block with a redacted `signature_delta`, three `text_delta` frames, the singleton `assistant` snapshot that arrives *before* `content_block_stop`, a `tool_use` whose input streams as two `input_json_delta` fragments, the `tool_result` in its own `user` record, and a terminal `result` carrying usage and cost. Session id is the deterministic placeholder `66666666-…`, uuids are sequential `dddddddd-…` placeholders, the tool id is `toolu_recorded_sdk_read_1`, cwd is `/work/repo`, and the thinking signature is `recorded-signature-redacted`. No credentials, tokens, home paths, hostnames, personal paths or real session identifiers are present. Used by `tests/claude_sdk_stream.rs`; evidence in `docs/design/evidence/claude-sdk-1.md`.
- `claude-transcript.jsonl` — a Claude session transcript in the shape written to `~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/<session>.jsonl`, recorded from a real 2.1.269 session on 2026-09-13 and reduced to one turn: the bookkeeping preamble (`last-prompt`, `mode`, `permission-mode`, a SessionStart hook attachment), a user prompt, a thinking block, a `Bash` tool call, its result, a sidechain record, a `file-history-snapshot`, and the final reply. Session and message identity are deterministic placeholders (`11111111-…`, `msg_recorded_transcript_*`, `toolu_recorded_1`), cwd is `/work/repo`, and the thinking signature is `recorded-signature-redacted`. No credentials, personal paths, or real session identifiers are retained. Used by `tests/terminal_promote.rs` for D-025 hydration.
- `claude-transcript-tools.jsonl` — the same transcript shape, recorded from a real `claude-pty` 2.1.270 session on 2026-09-13 whose prompt asked for `Bash`, then `Read`, then a summary. It keeps the structure a tool-heavy TUI turn actually has: commentary `text` and a `tool_use` split across two assistant records sharing one `message.id`, each `tool_result` in its own `user` record, a second tool in a later record, a `user` record whose array holds plain `text` rather than a `tool_result` (an interrupt notice), and the final reply. Session and message identity are deterministic placeholders (`22222222-…`, `msg_recorded_tools_*`, `toolu_recorded_bash_1` / `toolu_recorded_read_1`), cwd is `/work/repo`, and tool output is reduced to two short lines. No credentials, personal paths, or real session identifiers are retained. Used by `tests/pty_toolcalls.rs`; live before/after evidence is in `docs/design/evidence/pty-toolcalls-1.md`.
- `claude-transcript-skill.jsonl` — a real claude 2.1.221 session recorded on 2026-09-14 under `/tmp/remuda-p3/` for D-028 P3. The prompt was a single slash-command invocation of a throwaway `p3probe` skill, which is why the file holds the two records the origin classifier exists for: the `<command-message>` / `<command-name>` invocation markup and the expanded skill body (`isMeta: true`), **both filed under `role: "user"` though the human typed neither**. It also carries the non-conversation records a mapper must not choke on — `queue-operation`, five `attachment` subtypes (`hook_success`, `agent_listing_delta`, `skill_listing`, `auto_mode`, `command_permissions`) and `last-prompt` — and one assistant `message.id` split across a `thinking` record and a `text` record. Session id is `33333333-…`, message ids are `msg_recorded_skill_*`, uuids are sequential placeholders, cwd is `/work/repo`. No credentials, personal paths, or real session identifiers are retained. Used by `tests/transcript_origin.rs`; evidence in `docs/design/evidence/native-pty-3.md`.
- `claude-transcript-workflow.jsonl` — the same shape, recorded on 2026-09-14 from a claude 2.1.221 session whose prompt asked for one `Workflow` tool call. It is the fixture for the two user-visible defects in D-028 P3 feedback: the `Workflow` `tool_use` block carries only a `script` string (the title has to be parsed out of its `export const meta` literal), and the background task reports back as a **`<task-notification>` filed as a `user` record** carrying `origin: {kind: "task-notification"}` — the "结构化界面把追加的 prompt 也展示了" case. Also holds `system` records (`api_error`, `stop_hook_summary`) and a `toolUseResult` with the workflow's structured result. Session id is `44444444-…`, message ids are `msg_recorded_wf_*`, the tool id is `toolu_recorded_wf_1`, cwd is `/work/repo`. No credentials, personal paths, or real session identifiers are retained. Used by `tests/transcript_origin.rs`.
- `claude-transcript-tasktrack.jsonl` — sanitized records from real claude 2.1.221/2.1.272 transcripts (the foreground/background Agent pair was captured live through claude-pty on 2026-09-15 for c-tasktrack), plus a `<status>killed</status>` completion. It holds three Agent lifecycles: a synchronous foreground call (one Final result), a backgrounded launch (immediate `toolUseResult {isAsync:true,status:"async_launched"}` → later injected `<task-notification>` carrying the `<tool-use-id>`), and a killed launch (notification status `killed`). Tool ids are deterministic `toolu_recorded_task_*`, session id `55555555-…`, prompt text reduced, no credentials or personal paths. Used by `tests/tasktrack_fold.rs`; evidence in `docs/design/evidence/task-track-2.md`.
- `effort-21272/effort-walk-21272.jsonl` — verbatim subset of a real claude **2.1.272** PTY session recorded on 2026-09-15 by `examples/effort_probe.rs` (`PROBE_DIR=/tmp/remuda-r-effortsync2-probe3`) for effort-sync-2: a low baseline turn, `/effort xhigh` + `/effort max` (dialog dismissed → `Kept effort level as xhigh`) + `/effort ultracode` (accepted) + `/effort high` (accept; ultracode exits) + `/effort bogus` (invalid), each with its slash `<command-name>/effort</command-name>` user record and the sibling `<local-command-stdout>` verdict, plus the `ultra_effort_enter|exit` attachments 2.1.272 rides on the next prompt. Only `user`/`assistant`/`ultra_effort_*` records retained; session ids are the probe's throwaway uuids under cwd `/tmp/remuda-r-effortsync2-probe3/ws`, no credentials. `effort-reject-21272.jsonl` is the isolated Esc + invalid-arg record pairs. the full capture, hook timeline and timing marks stay in the probe's `$PROBE_DIR` (regeneratable). Evidence: `docs/design/evidence/effort-sync-2.md`.
